title: OmoBench benchmark run v1
description: The normalized, reproducible result summary submitted alongside raw benchmark evidence. Version 1.0 is the original contract, unchanged. Version 1.1 adds serving-environment, transport, weight-identity and tokenizer-identity metadata. Every 1.1-only property is forbidden on a 1.0 result, so a stored 1.0 bundle keeps exactly the meaning it was written with and never acquires a fact nobody collected.

schema_version.description: 1.0 is the original contract. 1.1 adds environment (runner, serving, transport) and model.served_model_id / model.weights / model.tokenizer / model.catalog_status. A 1.0 result is never upgraded in place: an absent fact stays unknown rather than being reconstructed.

run_id.description: Unique ID for this individual execution session.

configuration_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of normalized model (including source, when supplied), runtime, hardware, driver, arguments, and profile metadata. Deliberately excludes the top-level execution_device: hardware.gpus (always empty for a cpu run) already separates cpu and gpu configurations, so a legacy result predating execution_device and a freshly packaged, otherwise-identical gpu result still fingerprint identically.

execution_device.description: What performed inference for this run: cpu or gpu. This is a contributor declaration, not independent proof of execution. Absent on results published before execution-device tracking; those are treated as gpu for backward compatibility.

environment.description: Schema 1.1 only. Separates the environment that ran the benchmark from the environment that served the model, and records how requests travelled between them. Absent on a 1.0 result, where none of it was ever collected.

relationship.description: How the two environments are arranged. 'same-host': one machine and one operating system did both. 'windows-host-wsl-runner': the model server runs on the Windows host and the benchmark runner runs in a WSL2 distribution on that host. Any other arrangement is not representable here and is not supported for publication.

runner.description: The machine and operating system that ran GuideLLM. On a bridged run this is the WSL2 distribution, and it is deliberately not the serving hardware: what WSL can see about its host is not evidence about what served the model.

accelerators.description: Every accelerator this evidence can say something about, each with its own role and provenance. A device that did not perform inference is listed with role 'present-not-used' or 'unknown' rather than omitted or promoted.

mode.description: Where the weights were executed. 'cpu-gpu-offload' means some layers ran on CPU and some on one or more accelerators; detail then carries the split as the serving runtime stated it.

application.description: The desktop application hosting the engine, where there is one. LM Studio's release version is not the llama.cpp build inside it; both are kept, and neither is recorded as the other.

engine.description: The inference engine that executed the weights, and its build. When its version is known it is the same version as runtime.version.

settings.description: Serving settings that change the measurement: context length, how many layers were given to the GPU, batch size.

overhead.description: 'included-not-measured': the transport's own latency is inside every measured number here and has not been separated out. It is never subtracted.

execution.description: Schema 1.1 only. How this run was bounded, and whether the machine executed throughout it. Present only when the run itself recorded it: a bundle packaged from evidence collected before this contract existed has nothing to say here, and nothing may be inferred for it afterwards.

contract.description: Which set of execution rules bounded this run. Versioned so a change to what a run does is visible, rather than silently applied to results that predate it.

limits.description: Four limits, named for what each one bounds. They are not interchangeable: the inactivity timeout bounds the gap between two chunks of one response and is the runner's HTTP client's, while the request deadline bounds a whole request however lively its stream.

supervisor.description: Whether an independent timer had to stop this run, and whether asking politely was enough.

anchor.description: What the measurement window was counted from. The runner's ceiling starts at its first request, so loading weights and building a dataset belong to neither the ceiling nor the grace; 'run-start' means the run never reported a first request and the fallback applied.

interruption.description: Whether wall-clock time passed that this environment did not execute through. Evidence, never a correction: suspended time is never subtracted from a measured latency.

state.description: Ordered by how much each one claims. 'suspended' is confirmed, and only the kernel's own suspend record (CLOCK_BOOTTIME against CLOCK_MONOTONIC) earns it. 'clock-jump' is the wall clock disagreeing with the monotonic clock while the kernel says nothing happened: from inside that has two causes which cannot be told apart -- the environment was paused without being told, or the wall clock was stepped -- so it is reported as unexplained rather than promoted. 'gap' is a scheduling delay, where the clocks agreed and something merely did not get to run.

sleep_prevention.description: Whether the host was asked to stay awake for this run, and whether it agreed. A granted request is not a guarantee: a lid, a battery, a policy or a person can still suspend a machine.

id.description: Canonical catalog model identity, used for eligibility and comparison. Independent of source: it never changes when source is present or absent.

revision.description: Immutable model revision or commit SHA. Mutable labels such as main, master, or latest are rejected by registry validation. When source is present, this revision refers to source's own repository; it is not presented as a verified revision of id's canonical upstream repository.

source.description: The actual weights source, ideally the exact download URL pinned to an immutable revision and filename (for example a quantized re-export repository distinct from id's canonical repository). Optional: absent on results that predate this field, and on any result where the operator did not supply one; both remain valid and keep their existing interpretation, with revision then understood as id's own repository.

served_model_id.description: Schema 1.1 only. The identifier sent to the server's API, exactly as the server answers to it: an LM Studio alias such as 'deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-14b', for example. It is a serving alias, not an identity claim. model.id stays the canonical identity and is never derived from this string without a person choosing it.

catalog_status.description: Schema 1.1 only. 'proposed' means model.id is not yet in catalog/models and this bundle carries a model proposal for review. A proposal never makes a model catalogued.

weights.description: Schema 1.1 only. Where the bytes actually came from, kept apart from the canonical model id. A repository commit and a file checksum are different things here and are never interchanged.

repository_revision.description: An immutable commit of repository. Never a file checksum, and never a label that moves.

identity.description: Which route establishes this weight set: a pinned repository commit, or a hash over the bytes of the selected files for weights that have no public immutable revision.

content.description: The weight files themselves, each hashed from its own bytes. A sharded model lists every shard; manifest_sha256 covers the whole ordered set, so one shard differing is a different weight set rather than the same one with a footnote. A filename is never evidence of content.

tokenizer.description: Schema 1.1 only. The tokenizer that built and counted this workload, recorded because it decides the token numbers being compared.

loaded.description: 'loaded-before-run': OmoBench loaded this tokenizer in the runner's own interpreter before the benchmark started. 'not-checked': nothing loaded it here.

matches_served_weights.description: Kept explicit so that a successful load is never read as a match. A tokenizer that loads is not thereby the tokenizer the served weights were trained with, and nothing available to OmoBench can establish that it is.

server_description.description: Required when framework is openai-compatible-other; free-text description of the server. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character.

vendor.description: Optional GPU vendor. Absent on results published before vendor-neutral detection; never required, so old published results remain valid.

packaging.description: Schema 1.1 only. Present when a completed run was packaged again from saved evidence copied out of another directory, which is how a run that could not be packaged when it finished is recovered. It records what that derived bundle came from.

metadata_declared_after_execution.description: true when this bundle was built from evidence saved earlier, rather than packaged from the run's own directory. A hardware probe is refused on that path, because a probe taken then describes the machine as it is now and not as it was while the benchmark ran; everything supplied is recorded as declared.

evidence_sha256.description: The original evidence files, hashed where they sit, so the derived bundle can be shown to carry the same measurements rather than new ones.

gpus.description: Must be empty for a cpu run: no GPU performed inference. Detected-but-unused hardware belongs in the environment snapshot artifact, not here.

provenance.description: How this one fact was established. 'detected': a probe running on the machine that owns the fact read it -- which, for a serving host that is not the runner, means a probe run when the result was packaged rather than while the benchmark was running. 'server-reported': the inference server itself reported it over its own API. 'contributor-declared': a person typed it. 'unknown': nobody established it, and the value is then null. A fact is never upgraded between these, however plausible it looks.

fact_string.description: A string fact with its origin. A null value and 'unknown' always travel together: a value with nothing behind it would be invented, and an 'unknown' that still carried a value would be laundered of its origin.

role.description: What this device did for this run. 'inference' is a claim about execution, not about presence: detecting a card establishes the card, not that inference touched it, so a detected device nothing ties to the run is 'present-not-used' or 'unknown'.

provenance.description: How the device facts here (vendor, model, memory) were established. It says nothing about role, which is always a separate claim.
